prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling for the synthesis of aryl amines

statement.case_for: Palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling turned aryl amine construction from a case-by-case problem into a general, predictable operation. The advance is conceptual as well as practical: rational design of bulky, electron-rich phosphine and related ligands controls the oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination steps. Three decades of independent confirmation, daily use in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis, and a well-understood mechanism make it mature. Attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general catalytic method and the ligand classes independently and in parallel, and two names fit within the three-person limit without excluding a decisive contributor.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is that this is a continuation of the 2010 cross-coupling prize and may read as a second prize for the same idea. Only two members ranked it, so it has little committee support so far. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide aminations also complicate the priority story. If the committee wants a prize for a new conceptual direction rather than a mature method, B020 has a stronger claim and broader support.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation by induced proximity redefined what a small molecule can do, is mechanistically well confirmed, and is chemically robust and timely even without an approved PROTAC.
responses.response: I agree that B020 is the most original new modality on the list, and it is a serious alternative for me; the Crews and Deshaies concept is a real conceptual shift. My reservations are maturity and attribution. Clinical proof of the modality is still pending, and the PROTAC and cereblon glue strands are separate lineages, so a three-person prize splits them awkwardly (your Ciulli versus Linke's Handa). I do not think pending approval is disqualifying in itself, but a prize resting on the founding concept needs the committee to be sure the modality will hold up, and that is a bigger bet than for a method used for thirty years.

responses.point: C-N coupling is an original, widely adopted extension of the cross-coupling revolution, but its main weakness is that it may be seen as a continuation of the 2010 prize.
responses.response: This is the objection I take most seriously, but I think it underestimates the chemistry. The 2010 prize recognized C-C bond formation from organometallic partners. C-N coupling needed different mechanistic solutions, since amine binding, base choice and the slow C-N reductive elimination had to be solved with new ligand design. Hartwig and Buchwald are not in the 2010 group and their ligand-design logic is what made the method general. I accept that it is a closer call than a prize in an untouched area. I also respect your B061 case, which is clean in attribution and overdue, but its subject lies further from my expertise and I cannot judge its relative importance in the same way.

responses.point: B047 base editing is a clear, general enabling tool following from the 2020 CRISPR prize, with Liu as the cleanest single laureate; B020 is ranked first on conceptual originality.
responses.response: I agree that Liu is the intellectual driver, and a Liu-only configuration is more defensible than crediting Komor and Gaudelli, whom I listed in my opening. My concern is that the 2020 prize rewarded the programmable nuclease and base editing sits very close to it as a chemistry-driven refinement. The Kondo and Nishida priority claim for cytidine deamination also remains open. I would support B047 as a second part of a prize, but I do not think it displaces a mature synthetic method.

responses.point: Nitrogenase structure and mechanism gives a physically concrete mechanism for a hard redox transformation, with stable structural pictures confirmed independently over decades.
responses.response: I accept that B028 is mature and chemically concrete, and its attribution among Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe is the main difficulty I see. Which of three stays out is a real problem, because the work is spread across structure, kinetics and spectroscopy. The mechanism of substrate reduction is still partly open, and a prize that credits the structure while the central chemical question is unresolved is harder to justify than one where the chemistry is fully understood, as for C-N coupling.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat C-N coupling as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Whether Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work should be credited or acknowledged; the supplied text does not settle it.
Whether B020 is mature enough without an approved degrader drug and how its eight credited names would be allocated to three.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate is apparent from my profile: I have no documented tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or other shortlisted names. My mentor Masamune, and Chalmers, KTH, Lund and Tartu, do not appear on the shortlist. I sit on the committee with Lund colleagues Linke and Sparr, which is not a recusal issue for any candidate.
